articles.title: Bills Make Surprise Quarterback Move Before Jets Game
articles.summary: Josh Allen and the Bills are off to their best eight-game start since 1993. Buffalo has also made a quarterback move before facing the Jets.
articles.body:
Josh Allen and the Buffalo Bills are coming off one of their best starts to a season in more than three decades. Buffalo improved to 7-1 with a 23-6 win over the Minnesota Vikings on Monday, even after Allen was sacked four times and struggled to get much going in the first half.

The Bills eventually adjusted, getting the ball out of Allen's hands quicker before putting together a 15-play drive in the fourth quarter.

The quarterback finished with 234 passing yards, one touchdown and one interception on 21-of-31 passing. Allen also reached a career milestone with six carries for 15 yards, taking him past 5,000 career rushing yards.

On Saturday, the Bills elevated quarterback Shane Buechele from the practice squad, giving them another option behind Josh Allen and backup Kyle Allen. Buffalo also activated defensive back Jordan Hancock from injured reserve and released defensive back Te'Cory Couch.

28-year-old Buechele has spent time with the Bills before and knows the quarterback room. He went undrafted in 2021 after playing at Texas and SMU, where he threw for 3,929 yards and 34 touchdowns in 2019.

He later joined the Kansas City Chiefs and earned a Super Bowl LVII ring. A neck injury then cost him the 2024 season in Buffalo, but he returned to the field last year, completing seven of 14 passes in a Week 18 appearance for Kansas City.

Buechele returned to Buffalo and had a chance to play during the preseason, completing 26 of 38 passes for 196 yards in a 28-27 win over Pittsburgh.

Josh Allen and the Bills will face the Jets on Sunday at 1 p.m. ET at MetLife Stadium.

Week 10 is underway, and we're tracking all of the injuries before game time.

A.J. Brown (ankle/knee) could return this week after a multi-week absence when the New England Patriots face the Detroit Lions in Munich. Brown traveled with the team to Germany and, along with running back Rhamondre Stevenson (knee), has looked "pretty good" in practice this week, according to head coach Mike Vrabel.

Brown has been limited to three games this season and has been out since Week 7. He is listed as questionable for Sunday, along with Stevenson.

After sitting out last week while in concussion protocol, Deshaun Watson will be back under center for the Cleveland Browns on Sunday. Shedeur Sanders got the start against the New Orleans Saints in Week 9, but head coach Todd Monken announced this week that Watson is healthy enough to start .

Kansas City Chiefs running back Kenneth Walker III will sit out Week 10 with groin tightness. The NFL's second-leading rusher reported the issues on Friday morning and the team wants to "give him a week" to rest. Rookie running back Emmett Johnson will now handle first-team duties in Walker's absence.

Walker was listed as questionable on Friday's injury report.

Bhayshul Tuten (ankle/foot) practiced on Friday after sitting out this week for the Jacksonville Jaguars. The team's RB1 has 531 rushing yards and four touchdowns on the season. He was questionable last week after not practicing leading into the game against the Baltimore Ravens. The running back is not listed on the team's injury report this week.

Dallas Cowboys wide receiver George Pickens (hamstring) sounds ready to return after missing last week's win over the Indianapolis Colts. When asked if he'd be available Pickens told reporters , "When you turn that TV on, get some food, make sure if you have a wife or girlfriend, make sure you hug her, love her and when you turn the TV on you should see me."

Sam Darnold (ribs/quad) will miss another week for the Seattle Seahawks with Drew Lock (right elbow/oblique) taking charge against the Las Vegas Raiders this week. Darnold missed a Week 9 win after suffering the injuries the week before against the Chicago Bears.

Miami Dolphins quarterback Malik Willis (groin) and Los Angeles Rams receiver Puka Nucua (knee/turf toe) both were placed on injured reserve this week. Willis has been playing through a groin injury and, after undergoing an MRI, it showed he is dealing with a core muscle issue . Nacua sustained his injuries in Week 9 . He was later diagnosed with MCL and PCL sprains in his right knee and a turf toe injury.

articles.title: Llegan los recortes a los coches de etiqueta C: pagarán más en Madrid desde el 1 de enero
articles.standfirst: El Ayuntamiento ha incluido en sus presupuestos esta medida, que le permitirá recaudar casi cinco millones de euros... que saldrán del bolsillo de los conductores madrileños
articles.summary: El Ayuntamiento ha incluido en sus presupuestos esta medida, que le permitirá recaudar casi cinco millones de euros... que saldrán del bolsillo de los conductores madrileños
articles.body: El año 2027 ya está a la vuelta de la esquina... y viene con malas noticias para el bolsillo de algunos conductores, en concreto los que tengan un coche con etiqueta C (los gasolina matriculados a partir de enero de 2006 y diésel desde de septiembre de 2015) y paguen el impuesto de circulación en la ciudad de Madrid Porque a partir del año que viene, esos vehiculos van a perder una de sus ventajas: la bonificación del 10% al aparcar en la zona SER (Servicio de Estacionamiento Regulado). Es decir, cada vez que aparquen en el centro de Madrid, en las zonas verde o azul, la factura del parquímetro se incrementará a partir del 1 de enero ya que estos vehículos pasarán a pagar la tarifa completa. Así se recoge en el Presupuesto General 2027 del Ayuntamiento de Madrid, donde se detallan los ingresos previstos por esta partida que, lógicamente, es lo que les costará a los conductores madrileños: la recaudación prevista por este concepto se eleva a 4,85 millones de euros. Eso significa que, por ejemplo, un vehículo que tenga que estacionar una hora en zona de parquímetros pasará de pagar 1 euro a 1,10 en zona azul y de 1,85 a 2,05 en zona verde... siempre que se mantengan las mismas tarifas que en 2026 y también el precio variable (al alza, claro) que se aplica en las zonas que registran niveles de contaminación por encima de ciertos limites. El consistorio que dirige José Luis Martínez Almeida justifica esta medida al estar orientada a "contribuir a la mejora en la calidad del aire de la ciudad". Una calidad de la que los rectores madrileños presumen, ya que desde 2022 se viene reduciendo ininterrumpidamente el nivel de dioxido de nitrógeno (NO₂), el principal indicador de la contaminación en las ciudades. Eso sí, aunque las estacions de medición de Madrid están por debajo del límite de 40 microgramos de dioxido de nitrógeno por metro cúbico de aire, la legislación europea se volverá más restrictiva en 2030, ya que bajará ese límite a la mitad: 20 µg/m³. Los coches con etiqueta C son mayoría en España... y en Madrid, al menos si acudimos a los datos oficiales registrados en 2025, el último año completo. En concreto, en nuestro país había más de 10 millones de coches matriculados con estas características. En el caso de Madrid hablaríamos de más de medio millón de coches (de turismos, sin incluir furgonetas y comerciales en cuyo caso no iríamos por encima de los 800.000). En ambos casos, por encima del 40% del total del parque. En otro apartado del presupuesto, y como curiosidad adicional, se recoge la previsión de ingresos por multas para 2027 en Madrid. El Ayuntamiento de la capital estima que el año próximo recaudará un 4,4% menos para un total de 186 millones de euros (entre exceso de velocidad, estacionamiento indebido o acceso irregular a las ZBE). Eso supone medio millón de euros por día...

articles.title: Indian badminton hits new high! Lakshya Sen, PV Sindhu power historic 2026 season with record nine BWF titles
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: India's badminton contingent has enjoyed its most successful season on the BWF World Tour, with Lakshya Sen's historic Japan Masters triumph on
articles.body: NEW DELHI: India's badminton contingent has enjoyed its most successful season on the BWF World Tour, with Lakshya Sen's historic Japan Masters triumph on Sunday taking the country's tally to a record nine titles and four runner-up finishes in Super 300 or higher-level tournaments outside India in 2026.The previous best was six titles and three runner-up finishes, achieved in 2023. The latest milestone underlines the growing depth and consistency of Indian badminton, with players across men's singles, women's singles and doubles making their mark on the international circuit.Lakshya's triumph in Kumamoto was the latest highlight of a memorable campaign, with the Indian shuttler becoming the first from the country to win the Kumamoto Masters Japan title. The eighth seed fought back from a game down to defeat Japan's Koki Watanabe 13-21, 21-18, 21-14 in a 64-minute final at the Kumamoto Prefectural Gymnasium.The victory also gave Lakshya back-to-back World Tour titles after his triumph at the Hylo Open in Germany earlier this month."It feels very good to win a title here. Last year, I reached the semifinals, so I am happy that I could better that result. This is my second title back-to-back and I would love to continue this form," Lakshya said after his victory.Lakshya, Sindhu headline India's singles successLakshya and two-time Olympic medallist PV Sindhu have been at the forefront of India's impressive singles campaign in 2026, winning two titles apiece.Sindhu enjoyed a particularly productive season, winning the Japan Open, a Super 750 tournament in July, before adding the Hylo Open Super 500 crown in November. She also reached the final of the French Open, another Super 750 event, in October.Lakshya, meanwhile, won the Hylo Open and Japan Masters titles in consecutive tournaments. His campaign also featured a runner-up finish at the prestigious All England Open, a Super 1000 tournament in March.His Hylo Open triumph came against Indonesia's Jonatan Christie, whom he defeated 21-17, 21-10 in the final to claim his seventh BWF World Tour title and second crown at the tournament.The two successive titles have also strengthened Lakshya's prospects of qualifying for the BWF World Tour Finals, scheduled to be held in China from December 9 to 13.India's other runner-up finish in singles came through Kidambi Srikanth, who reached the final of the US Open, a Super 300 tournament.Satwik-Chirag, emerging shuttlers add to India's record haulThe men's doubles combination of Satwiksairaj Rankireddy and Chirag Shetty also played a significant role in India's record-breaking season.The pair captured two prestigious Super 750 titles, winning the Singapore Open in May and China Masters in September. They also finished runners-up at the Thailand Open in May.India's emerging women's singles players further strengthened the country's impressive tally. Devika Sihag won the Thailand Masters (Super 300) in January-February, Tanvi Sharma triumphed at the Taipei Open (Super 300) in July-August, while Ashmita Chaliha claimed the Korea Open (Super 300) title in August.Women's singles proved to be India's most successful discipline in terms of title wins, accounting for five of the country's nine crowns, including Sindhu's two victories.With nine titles and four runner-up finishes, Indian badminton has now set a new benchmark on the BWF World Tour, surpassing its previous best and making 2026 its most successful season by this measure.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: India’s Under-19 Asia Cup win over Pakistan marred by post-match aggression
articles.summary: India beat Pakistan by one wicket in a thrilling comeback in the final but follow it up with unsporting behaviour.
articles.body:
India have beaten Pakistan by one wicket in a nail-biting final of cricket’s Under-19 Asia Cup in Oman, but the comeback win was overshadowed by an on-field display of aggression and heated outbursts from the winning side.

The thrilling final on Saturday swayed between the two South Asian rivals before India scripted a last-ball win at the Oman Academy Cricket Ground in Al Amerat on the outskirts of the capital, Muscat.

Facing a steep target of 338 in the 50-over match, India staged a remarkable turnaround after slipping to 252-8 in the 42nd over as Manal Chauhan and Mohit Ulva rescued the run chase with a vital 57-run partnership for the ninth wicket.

The pair’s heroics gave India a record-extending ninth Under-19 Asia Cup title and their first one since 2021.

However, the winning side’s post-match celebrations quickly took an ugly turn as the players seemed to target Pakistan’s players with aggressive gestures that were later condemned by former cricketers and Indian fans on social media.

One Indian player was seen yelling and gesticulating angrily in the face of Pakistan wicketkeeper Hamza Zahoor, who did not respond to the aggression. Others kicked their legs in the direction of the Pakistan dressing room while the Indian team management tried to hold back the players.

India were lauded for their never-say-die spirit that saw them through but faced criticism for unsportsmanlike conduct.

Former Pakistan cricket captain Mohammad Yousuf emphasised the weight players carry when they step onto the pitch.

“You are not just representing your country. In fact, you are representing your upbringing, the values and the ethics your parents taught you as a child,” he wrote in a post on X.

“Therefore, always remain respectful and composed, whether in victory or defeat. True sportsmanship is reflected in the way you conduct yourself, regardless of the outcome.”

Former Indian cricketers and heads of state praised the team’s win but did not condemn their behaviour although several Indian cricket fans shunned the “uncalled-for” demeanour.

“India and Pakistan may be adversaries, and cricket may be fiercely competitive, but that is no excuse for such uncouth, crass and downright disgusting behaviour,” one Indian supporter wrote on X.

“The behaviour on display was a reflection of the culture of leadership this country has normalised. It’s a cricket match, not a war.”

“A country’s sporting culture is reflected not just in how its players win, but also in how they treat those who lose.”

Both sides skipped the customary post-match handshake, which has become a recurring feature in Pakistan-India cricket matches after political tensions spilled onto the pitch over the past year.

Last year, then-Indian captain Suryakumar Yadav and his players refused to shake hands with Pakistani team members during an Asia Cup clash in September and also decided not to accept the trophy from Asian Cricket Council (ACC) President Mohsin Naqvi, who also serves as Pakistan’s interior minister.

When Pakistan faced India in the ICC Women’s World Cup 2025 in Sri Lanka, the teams steered clear of handshakes and repeated the practice at the ICC Women’s T20 World Cup this year in England as well as their group-stage match in the Women’s Asia Cup.

In September, the India women’s team refused to accept the trophy from Naqvi after winning the Asia Cup final in Dubai, United Arab Emirates.

Chauhan, Ulva heroics lift India to victory

On Saturday, lower-middle-order batter Chauhan’s 47 from 32 balls revived India’s run chase while Ulva guided India home with an unbeaten 49 off 26 deliveries and was the final-ball hero for his side as he hit a boundary when they required three runs to win.

“This tournament had not gone well for me, but I had belief that I would be able to deliver today,” Ulva said after the match. “I needed Manal’s support, which he provided.

“I knew it was my day and that I would take my team over the line. Number 10 has been a very lucky number for me as all my runs have come from here.

“We had belief in our batting that we could chase this down. This was a flat wicket, and we kept telling ourselves that if they could score this many, then we could too.”

Pakistan posted 337-9 after winning the toss and electing to bat. Opener Usman Khan led the scoring with 107 off 111 balls while Abdul Qadir made 80 and captain Farhan Yousaf scored 63.

India’s reply was built on a strong platform laid by captain Lakshya Raichandani, who scored 80 off 101 balls, and fellow opener Aaryavir Sehwag, the son of India great Virender Sehwag, who made 58 from 61 deliveries and struck nine fours and was named player of the tournament.

Aaryavir finished as the tournament’s leading run-scorer with 361 runs in five innings.

India’s lineup also featured wicketkeeper Anvay Dravid, son of former India captain and coach Rahul Dravid, who scored 19 runs.

articles.title: Athletes rewrite the rules as Dakar 2026 Youth Olympics come to an end
articles.summary: Hosts Senegal thrive, and exuberant athletes defy the shadows cast over the Games by politics and history.
articles.body:
Dakar, Senegal – At the last event of the Dakar Youth Olympics , sneakers shrieked across the floor as breakdancers faced off.

Baggy trousers carried national flags. B-boys and B-girls dropped into six-step footwork, spun through windmills and defied gravity in sudden freezes. Arms became legs, legs became arms, each move a challenge, each response a little more daring.

The competition on Friday, the last in the two-week games, was less about brute strength or speed than invention, creativity, balance and nerve. Each of the teenaged breakers was part gymnast, part basketballer, part boxer all at once, and they brought a fitting energy to the end of a Youth Olympics held on the world’s youngest continent.

Before Senegal became the first African country to host an Olympic event, France’s development agency lent the already heavily indebted West African country 80 million euros ($88m) for sporting facilities for the games. It came as young people across the region are increasingly questioning the former colonial power’s lingering influence.

At Dakar’s railway station, I watched French police helping secure the event. Above them stood a statue of two bronze soldiers – one African, the other French. The African one, named Demba, represents the colonial troops who fought and died for France during World War I. The French one, named Dupont, rests an arm on his shoulder, a gesture of fraternity that others see as colonial paternalism.

Beneath their gaze, politics and history still cast shadows over the games.

At the first swimming medal ceremony I attended, Russia’s 17-year-old Serafima Fokina stood on the podium, gold around her neck, singing her national anthem. Some spectators rose. Others remained seated.

For Russian athletes and their supporters, it was a moment of enormous symbolism: The Russian flag and anthem were back at an Olympic event for the first time since the country’s suspension after its full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022.

Israel competed too despite its genocidal war on Gaza. A Senegalese man was arrested over a video opposing its participation that authorities described as threatening.

The International Olympic Committee (IOC) insists on political neutrality, a principle it considers fundamental to the Olympic spirit.

“Youth athletes should not be held accountable for the actions of their governments,” the IOC said, arguing that sport offers them access to hope.

But neutrality is a delicate ideal in a world divided by war, and the flags they carried can never be separated from the conflicts beyond the podiums.

For Palestinian swimmer Alma Shaat, representing her country carried a different weight. She had a message for the children of Gaza.

“Any little girl in Palestine right now, specifically Gaza, I would tell her … to continue following her dreams,” she told me. “She’s not doing it only for herself, but she’s doing it for the people in Gaza and in Palestine.”

Senegal outperform France as China tops medal table

China ended up topping the medals table with 18 golds. Japan were second on 11 golds and Russia third with eight.

Eighty Senegalese athletes had travelled not to France or the United States but to China to train before the fames, part of China’s soft diplomacy. For Senegal it paid off – they finished sixth, five golds to their name, ahead of France.

At her final news conference of the games, International Olympic Committee President Kirsty Coventry fought back tears. The Zimbabwean, who is the first African and first woman to lead the IOC, had helped bring the games to Dakar.

“I am so proud. I’m so grateful,” she said.

Yet it did not all go smoothly. At the Olympic village, the real test of unity came with the heat as athletes stayed in university dormitories without air-conditioning.

Outside the arenas, not everyone could get in. Events sold out. Transport was costly. But neighbourhood sports offered another way to join the celebrations in a city where children play football in the streets, and wrestlers train on the beach.

And sometimes divisions appeared to matter more than national pride.

I overheard a French-speaking Swiss journalist dismiss the prospect of covering a medal won by a German-speaking Swiss athlete. He also complained about the timing of events and the Olympic quota system, which limited participation to one athlete per country per event while giving greater representation to African nations.

But his complaints seemed strangely out of touch with the joyful spirit of the athletes, who were busy rewriting the rules. They had taken hold of the microphones and the cameras themselves. Each became a broadcaster, telling their stories through Instagram and TikTok, reaching audiences well beyond the television networks.

Back at the breakdancing finals, China’s Holy Rain faced Saturn of Chinese Taipei – two teenagers, one from mainland China, the other from Taiwan, dancing out their rivalry.

Amid the roar of the crowd, one spectator leaned towards another and shouted into his ear: “Imagine if their leaders could do the same.”

In the end, Japan’s Hiyo beat Ukraine’s 14-year-old Nikastar for the gold and Spain’s Mini Ali took bronze against Morocco’s Nawel.

Beneath their flags, rivals battled to the sound of hip-hop, then embraced. The flags remained. So did the divisions they represented. But for a few beats, neither seemed to matter.

articles.title: Ranking WWE and AEW's 10 Best Active Factions
articles.summary: Wrestling stables have long stood as the bed rock of the greatest wrestling stories of all time.
articles.body:
Wrestling stables have long stood as the bed rock of the greatest wrestling stories of all time.

From The Four Horsemen to NWO and beyond, these alliances help everyone involved to thrive when a stable is successful.

The modern wrestling landscape of WWE and All Elite Wrestling still rely on the importance of stables, even if the concept has somewhat fallen out of favor.

Who are the greatest active stables in WWE and AEW? Check out the list below.

A stable in wrestling is typically defined as three or more wrestlers with common goals, allies and/or adversaries.

A successful stable should be one that has been together for a while and not just aligned for one story.

The best stables have a clear name and theme that keeps them together and has brought multiple members success.

While stables typically start at three members, the AEW men's division has a trios division with plenty of three-man alliances that would not be typically considered a true stable.

The focus of this list is groups with notable history together, allying with common purpose not win just one title but multiple while taking the fight to other wrestling alliances.

The Vision: Bron Breakker, Bronson Reed, Logan Paul, Austin Theory and Maxxine Dupri

The biggest name group not included on this list, The Vision is struggling to stay together. While all talented stars, this group holds no gold and seem more likely to hold each other back from future success without Paul Heyman behind them.

The Opps: Samoa Joe, Hook, Katsuyori Shibata, Action Andretti, Anthony Bowens

While The Samoan Submission Machine is undeniable, this group has never truly clicked. With Bowens possibly gone from AEW as well, the group loses its most intriguing star outside of Joe.

Los Perros del Mal: Daga, Angel, Berto and Karmen Petrovic

This is primarily a list focused on WWE, and Los Perros del Mal have yet to break through beyond AAA. However, this is a group building a strong dynamic that could eventually break through to Raw or SmackDown.

While this is the only named and established stable in the women's division, Thekla, Blue and Hart have made their name enough to be included on this list.

Thekla's run as AEW women's world champion carried the women's division in the absence of Toni Storm, and The Toxic Spider is still a perennial world title contender.

Blue and Hart have consistently fought to capture the Women's World Tag Team Championships, and it would be a surprise if The Sisters of Sin are not AEW champs in 2027.

At the moment, the only gold this group holds are from World Wonder Ring Stardom, but that has led to more Stardom talent seeking them out in AEW.

Ideally, The Triangle of Madness would add more names to their ranks soon, but that would required a modified name. The Madness could be a simple correction.

Leader: Jacy Jayne (Women's United States champion)

Similar to the Triangle of Madness, Fatal Influence feels like the only women's stable truly trying to make a real splash in WWE.

Since arriving, Henley and Reid have won and lost the Women's Tag Team Championships, and Jayne holds the Women's United States Championship with confidence.

Is this a group that could truly challenge the top names in WWE? That remains to be seen, but Fatal Influence has caused problems for two former top champions, Charlotte Flair and Alexa Bliss, recently.

Unlike Jade Cargill and her Baddies, this is a cohesive trio without as strong an obvious hierarchy, and there is room for growth if WWE wanted to find a fourth for the alliance.

Raquel Rodriguez (Women's intercontinental champion)

The Judgment Day should be higher on this list because of the success of the long-standing group, but this stable has never felt less relevant.

Dirty Dom and JD have lost repeatedly as the last two men remaining in Judgment Day.

Liv, Raquel and Roxanne are a strong trio of women that currently hold complete control of Raw's women's division. However, it has not been an entertaining run.

It often feels like WWE is forcing Liv on a talented women's division rather than choosing fresher names.

It would not be surprising to see Iyo Sky and Becky Lynch take both titles in the coming weeks from Judgment Day, possibly pushing the group to turn against each other again.

Long past are the dominant reigns of Rhea Ripley and Damian Priest in Judgment Day, and a complete creative revamp would be needed to make this group seem scary again.

Leader: Will Ospreay (AEW men's world champion)

Andrade El Idolo (Casino Gauntlet contract holder)

The Brawling Birds - Jamie Hayter and Alex Windsor

Crossover from New Japan Pro-Wrestling: Francesco Akira and HENARE

From a pure success metric, United Empire should be much higher on this list.

Most of the names on this list are dominant competitors with championship pedigree, and Ospreay and Andrade are in the world title conversation.

However, this barely feels like a stable. While they all came together to help The Aerial Assassin overcome The Death Riders, these competitors barely work together.

In particular, while Ospreay regularly teams with the NJPW side of United Empire, he did not even team with a single member of the AEW UE team inside Blood & Guts.

Speedball checks on and teams with Andrade. Hayter and Windsor are an inseparable alliance. It is the leader that is not making this feel like a real stable.

The most interesting dynamic for this group is Ospreay's ongoing rivalry with NJPW UE leader Callum Newman in NJPW, which has not fully spilled over to AEW.

Once upon a time, The Conglomeration was the best babyface alliance in AEW, and the group still finds regular success.

Freshly Squeezed is constantly evolving and is one of AEW's biggest stars. O'Reilly and Strong could use more wins on their record but are constantly relevant.

The most successful member of The Conglomeration recently has been Willow, who is one of the best in the AEW women's division and only recently lost the AEW Women's World Championship.

If Takeshita formally joins the group and the group can bring back multiple injured stars, The Conglomeration could quickly rise up these ranks again.

This is the most prospective ranking of any stable on this list. 946 is still a new group that have made a massive splash early.

However, no one in this group regularly wrestles on Raw, focused more on beating down and running over The Bloodline backstage instead.

If 946 defeats The Bloodline though inside WarGames, it would instantly make 946 look like the most dangerous alliance in WWE.

It would not be surprising to see OTM win the tag titles even before the year is out, and Jaida could use some in-ring reps since she has done so little with 946 since her memorable Raw debut.

Keys could easily find himself challenging Roman Reigns for the World Heavyweight Championship soon, possibly on the Netflix Anniversary show to start 2027.

Melo and Montana are the biggest wild cards as they could be reliable midcarders or become the fall guys for Keys once 946 is more regularly wrestling.

It is all about potential, and 946 has more potential than any stable WWE has put together since The Bloodline.

The Dogs - David Finlay and Clark Connors

While The Cut is similar to 946 as a new alliance challenging the company's biggest stable, The Cut's history is heavily tied to The Bang Bang Gang.

White arrived in AEW in 2023 with Juice and quickly added The Gunns to make a crew that has reliably competed in the company over the past three years.

Austin, Finlay and Connors all signed with AEW in 2026 and added threat to a group that is now contesting The Death Riders better than anyone has in the past.

This culminated in a victory at Full Gear in Anarchy in the Arena over The Death Riders and Conglomeration.

Switchblade will go into the Continental Classic at the favorite to win, and this group becomes even bigger if the leader captures gold.

Kazuchika Okada (International champion)

Hechicero (CMLL world heavyweight champion)

RPG Vice - Trent Beretta and Rocky Romero

CMLL: Volador Jr. (NWA World Historic Middleweight Championship)

If this was just a question of the biggest stable in wrestling, The Familly would easily be the number one.

However, as funny a gimmick as it is that Callis is constantly looking for more men, the group is larger than it needs to be.

This causes certain stars like Cage and Clon to get lost in the shuffle for the stars Callis favors.

While it has helped Fletcher and Knight into major spots and Okada a reliable support for dominant title reigns, the dominance of this group as a whole ebbs and flows.

The Family did win big though in Blood & Guts, but The Protostar fell short in capitalizing to capture the Men's World Championship.

This is a massive group with major potential to dominate at any time, and few heel stables can take over AEW quite as reliably as The Family when booking calls for it.

Leader: Roman Reigns (World heavyweight champion)

No stable has defined the wrestling landscape quite like The Bloodline. However, this new-look Bloodline feels like a pale imitation of the original.

This is not the group that carried The OTC to the most days as world champion in the modern era at 1.316 days.

This is not the same group that saw The Usos define themselves as the greatest tag team in wrestling with all the gold in hand.

Instead, the group is relying on Reigns' continued dominance as WWE's star and the nostalgia for what was.

This could change if The Usos, Jacob and/or Sikoa win more gold. It could change if The Bloodline's story with 946 develops to a WrestleMania-level angle soon.

No matter all that though, The Bloodline is obviously still WWE's biggest stable and only a truly dominant run from 946 could unseat them.

Leader: Jon Moxley (Continental champion)

The Death Riders are the hottest act in AEW, and it is not that close a conversation.

Even with a recent loss in Anarchy in the Arena, Jon Moxley is the Ace of AEW, rallying not just the team but all of AEW after the passing of Pac.

The way this team has rallied together makes them the most sympathetic stable wrestling has seen in a long time, and they will continue to be a favorite in any match they work together.

While Mox may see his Continental Championship reign end in the C2, it is hard to imagine him long without gold since he is one of AEW's most decorated.

Given their history, it is appropriate that Mox and Roman Reigns stand as the leading forces of the biggest stable in the two biggest wrestling companies in the world.

They may continue to fight to define their group as the most important in all of wrestling.

articles.title: Germany vs Netherlands: Nations League – preview, team news, predictions
articles.summary: Germany will likely need to win on Monday to reach the quarterfinals unless Serbia beat Greece away from home.
articles.body:
Who: Germany vs Netherlands What: UEFA Nations League, Group A2 Where: Olympiastadion in Berlin, Germany When: Monday at 8:45pm (19:45 GMT) How to follow: Al Jazeera Sport will bring you all the build-up from 16:45 GMT before our live text commentary stream.

Germany and the Netherlands head into the final Group A2 Nations League match hoping to secure their place in the quarterfinals.

Xavi Hernandez’s Netherlands side are practically through – barring a huge swing in goal difference – as they lead the table with 11 points after thrashing Greece 7-0 on Friday.

Jurgen Klopp’s Germany, who beat bottom placed Serbia 3-1 in their last game, know they will likely need a win to progress.

The Germans sit third with eight points, level with second-placed Greece but below them on their head-to-head record, which trumps goal difference as a tiebreaker in this season’s competition. Greece host Serbia, who have yet to win a point.

Germany cruised to a 3-1 win against Serbia in Belgrade on Friday.

The Germans forced Serbia’s Srdan Babic into an early own goal with Florian Wirtz and Brajan Gruda also scoring.

Babic made up for his blunder with a second-half consolation strike while Serbia finished with nine men after substitutes Vanja Dragojevic and Andrija Zivkovic were sent off late on.

Germany have now won twice, drawn twice and lost once in five games under Klopp.

What happened in the last Netherlands game?

Tijjani Reijnders netted a first-half hat-trick ⁠as the ⁠Netherlands thrashed Greece 7-0.

The Dutch ⁠were 5-0 up at the break with Crysencio Summerville putting the hosts ahead in the sixth minute before Reijnders ran riot and Jurrien ‌Timber notched their fifth before half-time.

Timber scored again just before the hour mark with Donyell Malen netting the final goal.

Germany looking forward to ‘final’ against Netherlands, Klopp says

Klopp says his side are happy to have set up a deciding match against the Dutch.

“We wanted to set up a final against the Netherlands in Berlin, and now we have it,” Klopp said.

“We now have the chance to secure qualification for the next round in our own hands. We want to show everyone that German football is in good hands,” he said.

“We have good players, we’re working hard and we want to show in these matches that we’ve learned, that we’ve come together and that we’ve developed as a team. And that was definitely evident [against Serbia].

“The atmosphere in the camp is good, but that brings nothing if nobody can see it on the pitch. Our first job is to show the world that we can play football.”

The Opta supercomputer has made Germany the favourites with a win probability of 43.5 percent.

The Netherlands were given a 29.8 percent chance of winning while a draw was estimated at a 26.8 percent likelihood.

Cody Gakpo volleyed in a stoppage-time equaliser to rescue a 1-1 draw for the Netherlands against Germany in their Nations League Group A2 opener on September 24, denying Klopp a winning start to his tenure.

The visitors took a first-half lead with Felix Nmecha slotting in from close range. Karim Adeyemi should have scored another, but he somehow missed the target from 5 metres (5.5 yards) out.

The Dutch upped the pressure after the break and repeatedly came close to an equaliser with Germany’s new number one goalkeeper Marc-Andre ter Stegen making several good saves. But their dominance finally paid off with Gakpo’s late strike.

Bayern Munich stars Jamal Musiala and Serge Gnabry are unavailable due to muscle problems, but Germany have no other reported injury concerns.

Frenkie de Jong has returned to Barcelona for treatment after he went off with a back injury during the win over Greece. Teun Koopmeiners looks set to replace him in midfield.

Captain Virgil van Dijk did not join the squad during this international break due to injury, so Tottenham duo Micky van de Ven and Jan Paul van Hecke are likely to start as centre backs.

articles.title: Trade Ideas for the Chicago Blackhawks Amid NHL Rumors
articles.summary: The Chicago Blackhawks look like they are in the middle of another lost season in a rebuild that seems to be going nowhere. They enter play on Sunday with one of the NHL's worst records at 5-13-2 following Saturday's 5-4 shootout loss against the Winnipeg Jets (where they blew a 4-0 lead), and are ahead of only the Vancouver Canucks in the league standings.
articles.body:
The Chicago Blackhawks look like they are in the middle of another lost season in a rebuild that seems to be going nowhere. They enter play on Sunday with one of the NHL's worst records at 5-13-2 following Saturday's 5-4 shootout loss against the Winnipeg Jets (where they blew a 4-0 lead), and are ahead of only the Vancouver Canucks in the league standings.

While expectations were low coming into the season, there was at least some hope from management that some progress would start being made. So far, it is not. That has not only put head coach Jeff Blashill on the hot seat, it should be doing the same for general manager Kyle Davidson (even if he did just get a contract extension after the 2025-26 season).

That, combined with the record, has put some pressure on management to start making deals, and the Blackhawks are widely reported to be interested in adding NHL help sooner rather than later.

It is a dangerous game because desperation is never really the best starting point for a roster move, but it seems to be where we are.

The Blackhawks are reportedly looking for scoring wingers and defensive help, so let's try to look around at what they have to offer and some players that could be available and try to come up with some trade ideas for them.

The Blackhawks have no shortage of trade assets, ranging from young players in the organization (Oliver Moore, Frank Nazar, Kevin Korchinski) to potentially three first-round draft picks in the 2027 NHL Draft class.

The Blackhawks' first-round pick that they own should be off-limits, given that it could be extremely high in the draft. If, by some chance, it is traded, it needs to come with significant protections and conditions.

They also have the first-round picks that previously belonged to the Florida Panthers and Edmonton Oilers, as well as two second-round picks and two third-round picks this year.

All of that should put them in the market for a lot of players who could be available.

There are just two big potential problems when it comes to any deals that might be trying to be made right now.

The first is the fact that they have to avoid the temptation to do something overly desperate and potentially damaging long-term. This is not a team that should be trading for players on the wrong side of 30, players who are past their prime, or players who are just being brought in to try and salvage a season that might already be lost.

The other potential issue: No-trade clauses. A significant portion of the NHL has no-trade clauses in their contracts, and any player who has the ability to block a move might use it if Chicago is the potential team. That's what a decade of losing and a rebuild that is stuck in neutral will do. They might have to focus on players that do not have any such protections and/or are still on entry-level contracts.

So, with all of that said, let's get into some potential options and trade ideas here.

Trading for Capitals Ivan Miroshnichenko

The idea: Blackhawks trade a second-and third-round pick to the Capitals for Ivan Miroshnichenko.

This is a pretty obvious potential target, given that Miroschnichenko wants a fresh start, is absolutely on the market, and is a young player who could be a potential long-term piece if everything clicks for him.

The question is whether or not it would be a good fit.

The Blackhawks have struggled bringing along some of their own young players, and it remains to be seen whether or not they can do even that, let alone somebody else's prospect that has yet to pan out.

Miroschnichenko has big talent and untapped potential, but has struggled to crack a deep Capitals lineup and has a very limited NHL track record. The Capitals were reportedly seeking a first-round pick for him, but that seems like a steep price for such an unproven player.

But he's still somebody worth being interested in.

The idea: Chicago trades center Frank Nazar, a first-round pick, and a mid-level prospect to Detroit for Simon Edvinsson

The Red Wings still have a lot of unsettled business they need to address, including the hiring of a new full-time general manager, trading Dylan Larkin, and figuring out what to do with unsigned restricted free agent defenseman Simon Edvinsson.

Edvinsson still seems to want a trade, and he would, in theory, fit the mold of a player who should interest the Blackhawks, especially as they look to strengthen their defense.

He's still really young; he's shown that he is an NHL player; his best days are still likely ahead of him; and he would be a big addition to a defense that has a lot of young, unproven talent that is struggling to adapt to the NHL game.

The Blackhawks also have some players and assets that could interest the Red Wings, including center Frank Nazar. Detroit is almost certainly going to be in the market for a young center as it deals with the inevitable trade of Larkin and the hole that already exists with his absence, and Nazar could be a centerpiece of a trade like this.

Assuming Chicago could put together an offer that intrigues the Red Wings, the issue would then become Edvinsson's willingness to sign a long-term deal with Chicago. But let's pretend he would, just for the purposes of this exercise.

The idea: Chicago trades defenseman Kevin Korchinski to Columbus for forward Dmitri Voronkov.

Voronkov's name has appeared in trade rumors, and he seems like the type of player who desperately needs a change of scenery and a fresh start.

He also checks a lot of the boxes the Blackhawks are looking for in terms of a talented winger with size.

Voronkov's career got off to a strong start in Columbus with 18, 23, and 17 goals in his three full seasons, making him seem like a big part of their long-term plan. But he seems to have fallen out of favor with head coach Rick Bowness and has quickly played his way into the doghouse.

Columbus had a similar situation play out with Egor Chinakhov during the 2025-26 season, and getting a fresh start with the Pittsburgh Penguins helped him find his game and start to play up to his potential.

Could Voronkov follow that path? It would be a worthwhile pursuit for a lot of teams, including Chicago.

The price would probably be draft pick capital, or perhaps a similar young player who is struggling and could use a fresh start and a change of scenery.

Chicago has a couple of players just like that, including defenseman Kevin Korchinski, whose name has also been floating in trade rumors.

The idea: Chicago trades forward Oliver Moore and a first-round pick to the Flyers for Owen Tippett.

Teams should be calling the Philadelphia Flyers, and if they are not yet doing so, they need to start.

Whether it is trying to see if there is any chance that Matvei Michkov could actually be available, or if it's trying to get a veteran forward like Travis Konecny or Owen Tippett, the Flyers could be open for business. Especially in the middle of a brutal start to the season that has seen them sink toward the bottom of the Eastern Conference standings and deal with some very obvious frustration.

While Michkov might not be attainable at this point, a player like Konecny or Tippett might be.

Tippett might also be the more attainable player for a team like Chicago since he has fewer trade protections, is two years younger, and makes $2 million less against the salary cap.

He also brings plenty of speed and size, while also having scored at least 20 goals in each of the past four seasons. Like most of the Flyers players, he is off to a rough start this season offensively, but has enough of a track record that there should be plenty of confidence that he bounces back. Especially when that 5.7 percent shooting percentage starts to inch its way back up.

The Blackhawks also have some assets that could be attractive to the Flyers, including the speedy and energetic Oliver Moore and plenty of draft pick capital.

articles.title: Fernández y Calvo ganan en Dubái y el número uno ya es cosa de dos
articles.standfirst: La joven dupla se llevó la final del P1 de Dubái por 7-5 y 6-1, cerrando matemáticamente las opciones de sus rivales
articles.summary: La joven dupla se llevó la final del P1 de Dubái por 7-5 y 6-1, cerrando matemáticamente las opciones de sus rivales
articles.body: Las opciones eran remotas, pero si Paula Josemaría y Bea González querían dar la campanada y acabar la temporada en lo más alto del ranking, debían ganar el P1 de Dubái. Sin embargo, se han encontrado con unas Martina Calvo y Claudia Fernández que se han llevado la final en tierras emiratíes, dando la sorpresa y dejando la pelea por el número uno entre solo dos parejas. Llegaban Paula y Bea precisamente de derrotar a las otras candidatas en semifinales: Ari y Ustero. Una victoria que les daba mucha confianza y que suponía mantener la esperanza de darle la vuelta a la clasificación. Enfrente, unas Martina y Claudia que aterrizaban en la final tras acabar con Gemma y Delfi, demostrando una vez más el excelso nivel que han mantenido desde su unión. Pese a que las que tenían más en juego eran Josemaría y González, no lo pareció en la pista: las de Semprún fueron a por todo igualmente. La paridad reinó durante toda la primera manga. ‘La Perla’ y ‘Dinamita’ aguantaron el tipo hasta llevarlo todo al 5-5. Ahí, un break definió el 7-5 inicial que acercaba a Fernández y Calvo a su tercer título. Si lo que reinó durante el comienzo fue la igualdad —con la curiosidad de que Claudia Fernández sacó tres veces seguidas por error—, en el segundo set fue todo lo contrario. La madrileña y la navarra estaban imparables sobre la pista y no dieron opción a sus rivales, que no encajaron bien esa primera manga en contra. Se pusieron con una gran ventaja en el marcador y solamente tuvieron que cerrar el partido con el 6-1 definitivo que les dio el trofeo en Dubái. Tercer entorchado para ellas desde que están juntas, evidenciando que son una pareja de futuro y presente y que la próxima temporada van a estar con casi total seguridad en la batalla por el número uno. Actualmente son las cuartas en cuestión, pero su nivel habla de que están para más y que van a ser una verdadera amenaza para el resto de duplas en la búsqueda de acabar el año en lo más alto. Por el otro lado, Paula y Bea se despiden de sus opciones de lograr precisamente ese objetivo en su primer año juntas. Tuvieron tramos de muy buen juego y resultados, pero han quedado relegadas al tercer lugar y sin posibilidades de asaltar el trono a falta de dos torneos. Temporada de altibajos para dos jugadoras que intentarán terminar el curso de la mejor manera para encarar el 2027 con buenas sensaciones.

articles.title: El Oporto no da opciones al Lleida y conquista su tercera Copa Continental
articles.standfirst: El Oporto se impone al Pons Lleida por 7-1
articles.summary: El Oporto se impone al Pons Lleida por 7-1
articles.body: El Oporto hizo valer su condición de favorito y arrolló este domingo al Pons Lleida (7-1) en la final de la Copa Continental, disputada en el pabellón Joan Ortoll de Calafell, donde el conjunto ilerdense solo pudo sostener el pulso durante los diez primeros minutos. Después de caer en la final de la pasada edición ante el Barcelos, el equipo dirigido por Paulo Freitas se resarció con una actuación incontestable para recuperar el trono continental y conquistar su tercera Copa Continental tras los títulos de 1986 y 2023. En el otro lado, el Pons Lleida no pudo culminar su sorprendente camino hacia el título, después de eliminar en semifinales al Barça, el equipo más laureado de la competición con 18 trofeos, en un vibrante 6-5. El conjunto ilerdense encajó así su segunda derrota en una final, tras la sufrida en 2021 ante el Sporting de Portugal (3-1). La resistencia ilerdense duró apenas diez minutos. Rafa Costa adelantó al Oporto y Àlex Ortigosa respondió para establecer el 1-1, pero el empate fue un espejismo. El conjunto portugués aceleró, castigó cada concesión del rival y se marchó al descanso con un 3-1 que encarrilaba la final. El guión no cambió tras la reanudación. El Oporto mantuvo el pie en el acelerador, desactivó cualquier intento de reacción del Lleida y convirtió la segunda mitad en una exhibición ofensiva. El campeón del mundo Carlo Di Benedetto acaparó los focos con cuatro tantos y lideró una goleada que puso el broche a la conquista continental del conjunto luso. 7 - Oporto: Malian; Costa (1), Di Benedetto (4), Carballeira, Alves (1), -cinco inicial-, Pinto (1), Mena, Manrubia, Nunes y Pais (p.s). 1 - Pons Lleida: Bosch; Giménez, Ciocale, Moncusí, Badia, -cinco inicial-, Miguelez, Ortigosa (1), Gabarró, Ballestero y Hugas (p.s). articles.title: Oregon’s big plays sink Michigan in defense’s worst performance this season
articles.summary: Entering Saturday’s game, Michigan’s defense hadn’t allowed more than 21 points in any game this season. Three big plays by the Oregon offense essentially pu...
articles.body:
Entering Saturday's game, Michigan's defense hadn't allowed more than 21 points in any game this season. Three big plays by the Oregon offense essentially put up that many points by themself. Throughout the 31-7 loss on Saturday, the Wolverines allowed chunk play after chunk play, some of which resulted in touchdowns and some of which kept momentum in the Ducks' favor.

Two minutes into the game, Oregon wide receiver Jeremiah McClellan made a double move in man coverage against Jyaire Hill. Hill held McClellan up but he still made the play, and Mason Curtis missed an open-field tackle that allowed the Ducks to put points on the board quickly to take a 7-0 lead.

"Just gave up some big plays in the first half. Got to execute better, be us at the end of the day and get back to work," Chris Bracey said postgame.

Then just over six minutes into the first quarter, Oregon quarterback Dylan Raiola lofted a ball up to wide receiver Evan Stewart, who caught the ball after beating Hill one-on-one in tight man coverage for a 38-yard gain. Although the pass wasn't a touchdown and the drive didn't lead to a touchdown, the pass came from Oregon's own 5-yard line and completely switched the field position. A three-and-out from Michigan's offense gave the Ducks the ball back at their own 36-yard line, which they took 10 plays to reach the end zone.

"(We) let their guys get behind us a couple times, missing some tackles on a couple of the big plays," Whittingham said postgame. "Like I said, they got outstanding athletes, and they're going to make a miss on occasion, and they're fast. They've got great contact balance. … So between that and blowing a couple assignments, that's what gave up the chunk yardage with our defense."

Another instance where Oregon got behind Michigan defenders was when the Ducks got the ball back with 50 seconds left in the first half and a 14-7 lead. On the fourth play of the drive, Ducks wide receiver Dakorien Moore found himself wide open for a 59-yard touchdown after a broken zone coverage from Smith Snowden, who bit down on a shorter route that was already covered by a defender.

"That's a cardinal sin in that situation, to let somebody behind us, and unfortunately we did it," Whittingham said.

"Everyone has their own assignment, and at the end of the day, when you try too hard to make a play, or you try to compensate for someone else's job, it costs you," defensive lineman Jonah Lea'ea said postgame. "That's the only way I can play it simply, honestly. But I feel like that was a big thing today."

While it was down the field passes that exposed Michigan's defense in the first half, it was runs and short passes that did so in the second half. On Oregon's first drive of the second half, Dierre Hill Jr. rushed to his left for 36 yards to set the Ducks up in the red zone. A penalty and sack pushed Oregon deeper in field goal range as they ultimately missed the kick, but the run started to take advantage of a missed tackle situation for the Wolverines.

Again in the fourth quarter, though, Oregon actually took advantage of the missed tackles. After Tommy Carr fumbled the ball and offensive penalties backed up Oregon's offense to the 49-yard line, the Ducks drew up a screen pass because they were in a 3rd-and-19 situation. Multiple missed tackles later ended in a touchdown for Oregon and what became inevitably the final blow and final explosive play given up by the Michigan defense.

"The biggest thing is probably tackling, especially on that last touchdown that we gave up, we're giving up too much easy stuff," Lea'ea said.

"When you start to press and try to do more than just your job, you're trying to do more than you need to, and that sometimes is a product of that," Whitingham started to say about the explosive plays as a whole. "I'm not going to say that's why it happened. Again, they're good athletes, they're going to make you miss on occasion. But I think a lot of our problems stem from just trying to do too much and just not playing within the structure or framework of the defense. When you say that, our defense has been lights out all year, so it's not like it's been a recurring problem."

Although not a recurring problem, and Michigan has relied on its defense often this season, that is ultimately what happened. Whether it was trying to do too much, missing tackles or missed assignments, the Wolverines' allowed explosive plays that decide the game.

articles.title: Tigers checking in on veteran closer RHP Raisel Iglesias, per report
articles.summary: The Tigers are probably “checking in” on a lot of piayers, of course.
articles.body:
Rumor fly fast and furious this time of year, and with the owners planning to lockout the players on December 1, cutting off free agency until a new collective bargaining agreement is reached, things have gotten off to a fairly speedy start. Of course, a rumor of interest could come from an agent trying to drum up interest in their client, or from a lower ranking executive just generally mentioning a player as being a fit. None of this means there's a signing imminent, but BBWAA writer Francys Romero noted recently that the Tigers have shown interest in right-handed reliever Raisel Iglesias. That's pretty vague, so I wouldn't get too sold on the likelihood of a deal, but we'll explore it anyway.

The 36-year-old right-hander has racked up 130 saves for the Atlanta Braves over the last four seasons. His recent peak was the 2024 campaign in which he posted a 1.95 ERA with a 2.65 FIP and was among the most valuable relievers in baseball. He hasn't been quite that sharp the past two seasons, but he's still a very good reliever and would immediately become the Tigers' top dog.

Iglesias has had a much wilder ride than most major leaguers. A budding young closer on National teams for his native Cuba, Iglesias was caught fleeing through the mountains to try and defect. He was detained briefly but upon release escaped again and made his way to Haiti. A tryout in 2023 in Mexico City convinced the Cincinnati Reds to offer him a seven year deal worth $27 million. They tried to convert him into a starter in 2015, but abandoned that project the next season and he played out his contract with excellent success until he was traded to the Angels in 2020. They subsequently dealt him to Atlanta, where he played the past four seasons. Last year, the Braves signed him again to a one year, $16M deal and he made the All-Star gave for the first time in 2026.

Iglesias has since put together a decade plus of good to great relief work with rare consistency. In all that time, he's posted an ERA over 2.75 just twice. Basically, he keeps the walks down, strikes out an above average percentage of hitters and doesn't have a notable issue with giving up home runs.

From 2020-2022, Iglesias hit a peak where he was sitting 96 mph and punching out over 30 percent of hitters he faced. He was never quite in the elite class, but he was certainly among the nastiest relievers in the game. Now he's just plain nasty, but it's still plus stuff with good command. He features one of the best changeups in baseball and it's a time tested weapon at this point.

Iglesias sits 94-95 mph these days and mixes plenty of sinkers in with his fourseam fastball, which is his primary pitch. It's a pretty unique set of fastballs in that neither pitch moves that much, but from a funky, low three-quarters, short arm slot, they're really hard to differentiate for hitters. Add to that a changeup that looks exactly the same as the fourseam-sinker combo and then disappears, and you have a pitcher that really baffles hitters, gets whiffs, and rarely allows them to land their A swing.

The fly in the ointment is that Iglesias will be 37 next year, and if you've read my concerns about Emilio Pagán, well Iglesias is better but the same fears as velocity declines and mileage adds up are present. We'll leave it at that. The Tigers have had no luck at all with older free agent pitchers.

Iglesias would fulfill the Tigers desire for a high leverage reliever who can handle either-handed hitters. He's tougher on lefties, but handles right-handers just fine too. He does occasionally break out his slider against right-handers, and while he only used it 7.5 percent of the time last year it's still a solid pitch in its own right. The changeup is just the monster weapon in this repertoire, and might help Iglesias to continue to age well despite losing a full mile per hour off his fastball over the past two seasons. So far he's held up pretty well. It's probably wise to expect at least a little continued decline, but even so he'll likely be the Tigers best right-handed arm unless peak Will Vest returns or River Ryan or another starter converts and dominates.

The other problem, is that while the Atlanta Braves went and spent bigger than expected to land RHP Evan Phillips, they may very well turn right around and offer Iglesias another deal. The Tigers are just interested. Probably a lot of teams are interested. The crop of good relievers this offseason isn't exactly huge, and several names are off the board already. At this point I'd be pretty happy to land Iglesias but there is probably going to be a fair bit of competition for him now.

Right now, I'd probably put a low likelihood of this rumor turning into Raisel Iglesias to Detroit. If only because there are no particular ties to the Tigers for Iglesias. Ben Clemens of FanGraphs suggests he'll get a one-year deal for $13 million, but also suggests that a lot of teams will be in on him. Those two things aren't really compatible. If the Tigers want him, something like two years, $24 million might be what it would take. Some certainty for a player as a very uncertain offseason begins might be the ticket to luring him to pick the Tigers over the one year, $16 million that seems likely. We'll see if they want him quite that much.

articles.title: Tennessee Titans discussion: Week 10 live chat during the Jaguars game
articles.summary: Can the Titans pull off a miracle?
articles.body:
If we are being honest, the Tennessee Titans don't have much of a chance against the Jacksonville Jaguars today. They are just two teams heading in opposite directions. The Titans were the biggest seller at the 2027 NFL trade deadline, while the Jaguars were the biggest buyer.

All eyes are on Cam Ward in this game. The Titans need him to build off of the game that he had against the Cincinnati Bengals two weeks ago, when he threw for 300+ yards for the first time in his career. He doesn't have to throw for 300+ again, but he does need to show the same command of the offense that he did in Cincinnati. If he can string together a few of those performances, the Titans can feel confident he is the guy moving into next season.

Somehow, the Titans got less healthy during their bye week. They will be without Carnell Tate, Peter Skoronski, Anthony Hill, and Cody Barton in this game.

articles.title: Aidan Hutchinson out of game after suffering knee injury celebrating a sack
articles.summary: Hutchinson's knee buckled awkwardly as he landed after jumping in the air to celebrate sacking Drake Maye, who was also knocked out of the game.
articles.body:
Lions defensive end Aidan Hutchinson has been ruled out of the game after injuring his knee celebrating a sack.

Hutchinson sacked Drake Maye on third-and-goal to end the Patriots' first offensive possession. Hutchinson then got up to celebrate, jumped into the air pumping his fist, and landed awkwardly. His right knee appeared to buckle.

Although Hutchinson was able to limp off the field under his own power, it looked like a potentially serious injury for Hutchinson, a Defensive Player of the Year candidate.

Maye was also injured when Hutchinson sacked him: Maye hurt his ankle and was ruled out of the game.

Injuries have affected both teams, but the Lions are in better shape with a 28-3 lead in the fourth quarter.

articles.title: Broncos mid-season awards: Team MVP, DPOY, ROY and more
articles.summary: The Denver Broncos have had several standout players in the first half of the 2026 NFL season.
articles.body:
The Denver Broncos are now nearly past the halfway mark of the 2026 season, and it's time to hand out midseason awards for the team.

At Broncos Wire , we are handing out team MVP awards, Offensive and Defensive Player of the Year, Offensive and Defensive Rookie of the Year and Protector of the Year. Check out our list of award winners below, and let us know if we missed anyone.

Despite missing two kicks in two weeks, Lutz has again been one of the most consistent players on the team. Lutz hit a game-winner in overtime against the Seattle Seahawks , and set the NFL mark for consecutive extra points made this season. Lutz has been a big part of the Broncos ' success, and will surely continue to play a huge role in Denver's future of the 2026 season.

Offensive Player of the Year: Pat Bryant

Bryant has been one of the most reliable pass-catchers for Denver this year. Even after a stint on injured reserve, Bryant's impact on the offense was especially evident in the Week 9 contest against the Carolina Panthers , when free agent addition Jaylen Waddle went out early in the first half with a concussion. Bryant is a young player who will continue to develop into an arrow in the quiver for quarterback Bo Nix.

Defensive Player of the Year: Zach Allen

Allen has quietly put up the kind of performance that many voters would consider for an All-Pro bid and a Pro Bowl campaign. Allen has been a force in the middle of the defense, disrupting the quarterback and blowing up the run game. One of the biggest leaders on the Denver defense, there aren't many players who can have the kind of impact he's had this season.

Offensive Rookie of the Year: Jonah Coleman

There's really no question about this one. Coleman has been far and away the best rookie on the team, simply because he's gotten the most playing time of any rookie on the Broncos ' roster thus far. Even after a stint on the injured reserve, Coleman has come back into the lineup with a vengeance, quickly running up the snap count and earning the No. 1 running back spot on offense.

Defensive Rookie of the Year: Sean Fresch/Tyler Onyedim

Fresch is technically a cornerback, so we're going to go with him. Fresch has been a great return man, alongside wide receiver Marvin Mims.

Draft pick Tyler Onyedim is the only other rookie to have played in a game this year, and only played 10 defensive snaps in the one game (Week 9) he has been active, but he forced a fumble on Panthers running back Chuba Hubbard in Week 9. If by the definition of a defensive player, then Onyedim wins the award.

Meinerz has had a penchant for flattening his opponents throughout the season. From blocking Aaron Donald to Princely Umanmielen, Meinerz has been a force on the offensive line, being one of the most consistent players throughout the year. Meinerz should be in the top two, if not the winner of the NFL's Protector of the Year award after being a finalist for the inaugural award in 2025.

What do you think? Did we miss anything or anyone? Let us know on Facebook and Twitter/X !

articles.title: Steelers vs Bengals live updates: TV info, live stream, odds for Week 10 game
articles.summary: Pittsburgh and Cincinnati are vying for control of the AFC North division in this primetime matchup.
articles.body:
For the Pittsburgh Steelers , their "Sunday Night Football" matchup with the Cincinnati Bengals on Nov. 15 is about more than control of the AFC North division.

It's about proving they can be a real contender in the AFC after years of one-and-done playoff exits.

Both teams enter the the matchup with 6-2 records. One of the Steelers' wins came against these same Bengals back in Week 3, when first-year coach Mike McCarthy and Co. prevailed by a 30-27 margin at Acrisure Stadium.

The Bengals have become one of the most dominant offensive forces in the league since. They've averaged 35.75 points per game during their current four-game winning streak.

The Steelers are on a four-game winning streak of their own, but have relied on solid defense and just enough offense to overcome the mostly unimpressive Indianapolis Colts , Tampa Bay Buccaneers, New Orleans Saints and Cleveland Browns.

Now fans will want to see that they can go on the road and take down a peer in front of a primetime audience.

If they do, that will foster belief that this team, led by veteran quarterback Aaron Rodgers, can be the first to win a playoff game for the franchise since 2017. If they lose, Steelers fans will mutter that nothing has really changed and that another early playoff exit may be the best they can hope for.

USA TODAY sports will provide live updates of the action from Paycor Stadium in Cincinnati.

articles.title: Behind Enemy Lines: 5 things to know about the Las Vegas Raiders
articles.summary: Join us on another journey behind enemy lines!
articles.body:
The Seattle Seahawks are closing out their old AFC West rivals reunion tour today with a road game against the Las Vegas Raiders . Seattle took care of the Chiefs and Chargers in convincing fashion, but narrowly lost to the Denver Broncos . Today's game will determine if the Seahawks finish with a winning record against their former division.

The Raiders may be old rivals, but this is a team the Seahawks now only play every four years or so. A lot has happened to both teams since they last squared off, which was a stunning 40-34 upset overtime loss at Lumen Field in 2022. Vegas bulldozed their way to 273 yards rushing and two touchdowns as a team. Now the Seahawks boast a legendary run defense, and the Raiders will be ushering in the new era with Fernando Mendoza at quarterback.

I spoke with my friend and colleague Levi Damien, the managing editor over at our sister site Raiders Wire , to get a better idea about this Vegas squad. My questions and his answers are below.

What can we expect from Fernando Mendoza in his first ever start?

I expect he will come in fairly confident and be pretty smooth running Kubiak's offense. And I expect him to make a couple nice throws that show why he was the number one pick. But I also expect the Seahawks defense to rattle him into a couple mistakes that will prove costly.

Vegas started red hot, now they're ice cold. What has caused this drastic collapse?

Quality of opponents. Plainly put. Their first three games were against the Dolphins , Chargers, and Saints . And their only other win was against the Jets. When they face any decent teams, their defense gets run through and their offense can't catch up.

Is there a position you think the Raiders have an edge over Seattle?

Tight end is the only position for the Raiders that is worth mentioning in terms of being better than their opponents. Brock Bowers is probably the best tight end in the league and his backup Michael Mayer is better than a lot of starters. In fact, it's probably not even fair to call Mayer a backup considering he starts at tight end while Bowers often lines up outside as a receiver.

Who is a non-household name Raider we should know about?

There is no single player who really stands out who isn't obvious (Bowers, Crosby, Linderbaum), so I will give you a couple who have played surprisingly well this season. On offense I'd say right tackle DJ Glaze has surprised. He had a terrible time last season under Pete Carroll's son as OL coach. This year he's doing pretty well keeping opposing rushers out of the backfield. On defense rookie safety Treydan Stukes has showed up well. He has a couple interceptions this season and quite a few nice pass breakups as well.

Don't see how the Raiders win this one. Not against that Seattle defense. And I have yet to see the Raiders defense slow down even the most beleaguered offenses, so I expect Drew Lock to be able to do enough to lead the Seahawks to the win.Seahawks 27, Raiders 17

articles.title: Everything Miami HC Mario Cristobal said after win vs. Duke
articles.summary: Miami head coach Mario Cristobal discusses the Hurricanes' 36-25 victory over Duke.
articles.body:
Again, first, I want to thank everybody that came out for homecoming. That crowd was awesome. Great to see so many familiar faces. I know it's a special time of year for alumni to be able to partake in the festivities in a game like that. And then really proud of our players, our coaching staff, really just got back to work right in the locker room last week, last Saturday, just kind of made a decision to get back to work. We have what we have. We're going to have some injuries, and we just got to find a way to get it done, and though that after the first two drives that our offense really got going, I think we scored about seven successive drives after that and found a lot of success on defense, albeit a couple explosive plays from them. Hats off to Duke , really good football team, well coached, tough.

Their running back is a really, really special player, but all really, really good, again, conference win. Conference football is playoff football. We always say it. So want to know what was accomplished.

Well, I would say I really don't think we have different depth than anybody else. I really don't. And I mean the roster size proves that. I think the development of some of the guys that have been in line for playing time showed up in some really critical spots. Poiser didn't play today. The guy's the ultimate communicator and player back there. Phenomenal player. Obviously, we're playing without Malachi and Max Buchanan, a bunch of other guys and OJ. Seeing those guys on the sideline, it makes you, but so are a lot of people. And so instead of sitting back and we just choose to go forward, find ways to get better.

On status of Mark Fletcher and Zechariah Poyser

Fletcher, I think, is going to be fine. I think he got nicked up in the first half. Feel good about Poyser this next week.

Well, I think a couple things. Number one, early on, a lot of self-inflicted wounds, right? Penalties putting us behind and off schedule. I think also the way that there's so much pressure and movement that you have to live with some of the short games or negative plays that come with that. You have to, but you still have to stick to the run. You have to find different formations and different ways to knock out the interior and cut off the edges. And we kept going back and forth. It's a little bit of a cat-and-mouse game, but we felt that we found ourselves getting some better push, getting downhill. And then our guys started breaking some big runs and taking over the game. But the fourth quarter is certainly very indicative of just a really good summer strength and conditioning, being able to move the line of scrimmage as such.

We'd like to close it out better at the end on defense, but I saw a lot of progress on defense, a lot of much better play at corner, particularly in man coverage. The interception by X certainly stands out, but all in all, just really proud of our team.

On defense holding Duke to three early points

No, that was awesome. To me, that was probably a difference in the game because we had a tough time getting things going offensively. And the last thing you want to do is let that side over there grab the momentum because they have a really good defense. Top in the conference, top-10 defense in the country. And so for them to come out and do that, it certainly set the tone for the game. It gave the offense a lot of confidence, and we worked our way through some of those early struggles on offense to start popping some touchdowns and some big plays. Early on, we were stuck in a red zone. We got ourselves, I think, three times, found ourselves stuck down there, and credit to them. They do a good job. But after that, I think it's a little bit more indicative of what we want to do and what we have to do.

On if Darian Mensah and Cooper Barkate had any extra motivation facing former team

I mean, I think there's always a little bit of that, but I think the majority of their motivation, their daily just want to and drive is solely based on winning and getting better. I do believe that. I believe that the narratives are more for the weak and the pageantry of college football and the excitement that builds, or narratives that build, but I have a tough time believing that that's really a part of anybody's process.

On holding up against Duke's defensive line

Well, obviously early we struggled. There were a lot of twists and games, and some of the concepts were a little bit further down the field. We had a couple holding penalties. So one thing we do is go back to work, and instead of throwing crap at our guys and jumping in with the insults we do, we go back to work and get better. And I think it's a testament to them, to Coach Dawson, to Coach Mirabal, that as the game went on, the offensive line got stronger, protection got better, and the running game started taking over. So it's a four-quarter game. We pride ourselves in strength and conditioning and what it can do for you as the game wears on. And I think it showed up today.

articles.summary: Welcome back to the Pentagon…
articles.body:
Location: Sandford Pentagon (Sioux Falls, S.D.)

Sunday's game will be televised on FS1 with Connor Onion and Shon Morris on the call. The game is also available online on the FOX One app.

Sunday's game will be carried on the Huskers Radio Network with Kent Pavelka and Jeff Smith on the call, including KLIN (1400 AM) in Lincoln, WOW (590 AM) in Omaha and KRVN (880 AM) in Lexington. The pregame show begins an hour before tipoff and will also be available on Huskers.com and the Huskers app.

Two high-octane offenses will battle this Sunday in Sioux Falls, as the No. 25/24 (AP/Coaches) Huskers take on Boise State in an early season battle of unbeatens. Tipoff from the Sanford Pentagon is slated for shortly after Noon (central) and the game will be televised on BTN and broadcast across the state on the Huskers Radio Network as well as on Huskers.com and on the official Huskers app. Sunday's matchup with Boise State has been sold out since tickets went on sale to the public in September with a sellout crowd of over 3,200 for the neutral-site contest.

Boise State comes to Sioux Falls with a 3-0 mark following a 111-79 victory over Oakland on Wednesday. The Broncos have been one of the most consistent programs on the west coast under Leon Rose, posting five straight 20-win seasons and averaging 22.5 wins per season since 2019-20. Rose is in his 17th year at Boise State and has guided the Broncos to the postseason in five of the last six seasons, including NCAA appearances in 2022, 2023 and 2024. The Broncos are in their first season in the new Pac-12, where they were picked sixth in the preseason poll. Boise State opened the season by scoring 132 points against West Coast Baptist before putting up 100 points in a 100-81 win over Butler.

Sophomore guard Aginaldo Neto has paced the Bronco attack, averaging 20 points per game on 54 percent shooting and 6.0 assists per game after averaging just 3.2 ppg as a freshman. Damari Wheeler-Thomas, a transfer from North Dakota State, is averaging 17.3 ppg on 57 percent shooting, while going 10-of-19 from 3-point range. In all, Boise State has six players averaging double figures and is shooting 53 percent from the floor as a team, including 41 percent from 3-point range, and committing just 8.7 turnovers per game.

This one will be interesting. Boise State has a very strong offense, much like the Huskers do. This will become all about Nebraska's defense and keeping Boise State off the offensive glass. These two teams can certainly go toe-to-toe from the 3-point line, so expect many shots to come from behind the arc. The Pentagon has been kind to the Huskers, as we have never lost there (knock on wood). Having said that, this could be the most talented team we've faced there.

As per usual, despite this being a "neutral" site game, this will definitely be a pro-Husker crowd. Hopefully nobody gets thrown out for handing the basketball to a referee with a slight bit of force. I felt bad for that guy; dude did nothing wrong. Refs are just pansies at times. Not like the guy was cussing him out. I like Nebraska's offense a little bit better, but if we can't control the Broncos on the glass, it could get rough. I think this is closer than the 9.5 points we are favored by. Score Prediction: Nebraska 91 Boise State 86
