articles.title: Detroit Lions Release Concerning Aidan Hutchinson Injury Update
articles.summary: The Detroit Lions have officially ruled out Aidan Hutchinson with a knee injury against the Patriots after a frightening first-quarter incident.
articles.body:
The Detroit Lions have received more concerning news regarding star defensive end Aidan Hutchinson, and it is certainly not what fans were hoping to hear.

The Lions have officially downgraded Hutchinson to OUT for the remainder of Sunday's matchup against the New England Patriots in Munich, Germany, due to a knee injury. The announcement came after Hutchinson suffered the injury while celebrating a first-quarter sack of Patriots quarterback Drake Maye.

Detroit originally listed Hutchinson as questionable to return, but the team's latest announcement confirms that his afternoon is over.

The Detroit Lions' official public relations account announced the news during the second half, providing the following update:

"#Lions Injury Update: EDGE Aidan Hutchinson (Knee) has been downgraded to Out."

EDGE Aidan Hutchinson (Knee) has been downgraded to Out."

As previously reported, Hutchinson suffered the frightening injury after jumping in celebration following a sack of Maye during New England's opening offensive possession.

According to CBS Sports' account of the incident , Hutchinson landed awkwardly following his celebration and immediately went down grabbing his right leg. He eventually walked off the field under his own power before receiving medical attention and heading to the locker room.

The Lions initially confirmed a knee injury but left open the possibility of Hutchinson returning. That possibility has now been eliminated for Sunday's game.

Lions Await More Information on Hutchinson

Losing Hutchinson for the remainder of the game is a significant blow to Detroit's defense, particularly given the team's existing injury concerns.

The former Michigan standout has established himself as one of the NFL's most dangerous pass rushers and entered Sunday's contest with six sacks this season. His ability to pressure opposing quarterbacks is a major part of what makes Detroit's defense successful.

The injury is especially frustrating because Hutchinson had already made an impact against New England. His first-quarter sack helped force a Patriots field goal, but the celebration that followed ended his afternoon.

According to The Associated Press , Hutchinson was able to walk to the sideline medical tent before making his way to the locker room for additional evaluation.

At this time, the Lions have not announced a specific diagnosis or provided a timetable for Hutchinson's return beyond Sunday's game. Being ruled out confirms that he will not play again against New England, but it does not establish how severe the injury might be.

For now, the Lions and their fans can only hope that Hutchinson has avoided another significant setback.

Detroit may be in control of the game against New England, but the health of its star defensive end has suddenly become one of the biggest concerns moving forward.

articles.title: Tenerife return to action after death of De Miguel
articles.summary: Tenerife play their first game since the death of striker Jesus de Miguel on an emotional day at the Heliodoro Rodriguez Lopez stadium.
articles.body:
Tenerife played their first game since the death of striker Jesus de Miguel on an emotional day at the Heliodoro Rodriguez Lopez stadium.

De Miguel died at the age of 30 on 3 November, a day after colliding with Andorra goalkeeper Jesus Owono during a home match in Spain's Segunda Division.

Tenerife beat bottom side Ceuta 2-0 on Sunday, with tributes to De Miguel paid both before and during the game.

Lengthy standing ovations preceded and followed a minute of silence before the match.

In the ninth minute play was stopped and a round of applause took place, while a video of De Miguel was shown in the stadium, as happened at all first- and second-tier games in Spain last weekend.

Tenerife fans displayed a banner that read: "Jesus de Miguel, 9, eternally blue and white."

Forward Nacho Gil opened the scoring for the home side in the 40th minute and celebrated by holding up De Miguel's shirt.

Gil revealed a message written under his shirt that read: "Demi, always in our hearts."

Neal Viereck scored four minutes from time as Tenerife ended a run of six games without a win. They are 14th in the table.

Tenerife's game with Granada on 7 November was postponed and the club invited fans to the stadium to pay their respects to De Miguel.

Owono was given a 12-match suspension by the Spanish football federation for the challenge which resulted in De Miguel's death.

The federation has ruled that the game between Tenerife and Andorra, which was abandoned seven minutes into stoppage time after the incident occurred, will not be replayed and the 2-2 score will stand.

articles.summary: Clemson quarterback Tait Reynolds got banged up on Saturday
articles.body:
Clemson got some tough news about starting quarterback Tait Reynolds on Sunday, Nov. 15.

According to Larry Williams of On3 , Reynolds suffered a ligament tear in his left knee against Georgia Tech on Saturday and will require surgery.

Reynolds completed one pass for three yards and rushed once for 24 yards before leaving the game. He was replaced by Trent Pearman, who was then replaced by Christopher Vizzina.

To make matters worse, Vizzina suffered a concussion late in the game and had to be taken to the hospital. Clemson lost 20-6, dropping its overall record to 6-4.

How has Tait Reynolds played this season?

Reynolds, a true freshman, has appeared in all 10 games for the Tigers this season, compiling 1,449 passing yards, three touchdowns and four interceptions. He took over the starting role in September and had his best game against the Florida State Seminoles on Halloween. In a 36-24 win, Reynolds finished with 189 yards and two touchdowns. He also rushed for 85 yards and a touchdown.

Clemson has two games left in the 2026 season and will play Duke on a short week Friday before playing in-state rival South Carolina.

articles.title: Campos helps Kalaheo romp past Pac-Five in D-II state playoffs
articles.summary: The Mustangs are galloping into the semifinals. Reserve running back John Campos rushed for 181 yards and touchdowns of 28, 7, 2 and 2 yards on 26 carries as...
articles.body:
The Mustangs are galloping into the semifinals.

Reserve running back John Campos rushed for 181 yards and touchdowns of 28, 7, 2 and 2 yards on 26 carries as unbeaten Kalaheo overwhelmed Pac-Five 61-21 on a windy Saturday night at Skippa Diaz Stadium.

Kalaheo (11-0) travels to play Kamehameha-Maui on Friday in the semifinal of the Hawaii Army National Guard/HHSAA Division II Football State Championships.

"We're trying to fly on Thursday," Kalaheo coach Jaymason Lee said. "This is my first time trying to plan it, this state-tournament thing. We're trying to figure out the logistics of the flight, the hotel, the transportation. There's a lot of work to do, but I'd rather be doing the work than watching it."

The short week means the Mustangs staff will get to work early and ahead of the curve.

"I like to look at (game video) right away, so we're going to upload it, break it down, however long it takes, 2 in the morning while it's still fresh," Lee said. "Get the notes down because it's going to be a fast week."

A flu bug hit the team all week, which led Lee to hold starting RB Marquez Mellor out. He was in uniform just in case.

"He kind of had it the worst. We had a couple of linemen sick. I just got over it," Lee said. "Marquez is such a team player. He said, 'Coach, if I can't play, I trust in Johnny Camp to get it done.' "

Kalaheo, the OIA champion, took all Pac-Five could give. The Wolfpack, representing the ILH, tied the game in the second quarter, taking advantage of three early Kalaheo turnovers. From that point on, however, Kalaheo's offensive front took command at the line of scrimmage.

"Pac-Five is always going to play tough and smart because of their staff," Lee said. "I felt like they're kind of like us in ways. They don't have their own field. I don't know how their locker room is. Less facilities. Just trying to make things work and try to compete. I knew they were going to come out and do exactly what they just did."

Pac-Five wide receiver Avari Zion-Branch did what he could against double coverage. The 6-foot-2, 182-pound senior finished with 12 receptions for 199 yards, including TDs of 7, 5 and 72 yards. The finality of being a four-year Wolfpack player hit hard.

"It's a lot of emotions. I'm going to miss my team," Zion-Branch said. "This is a place where we have a culture and get to know our teammates from all our schools."

Kalaheo won the coin toss, took the field on defense and sacked Pac-Five QB Brady Shimabukuro. With the wind at their backs, the Wolfpack managed a 34-yard punt that was returned 14 yards to the Pac-five 30-yard line.

Five plays later on fourth-and-2, Zayne Farley took the snap and snaked his way up the middle for a 22-yard TD run.

After Pac-Five's second punt, Kalaheo drove 41 yards in two plays. Campos rumbled up the A-gap, bounced off defenders and scored on a 28-yard TD. Kalaheo led 14-0 with 6:16 left in the first quarter.

The Wolfpack drove 62 yards in 11 plays to pay dirt. Shimabukuro found Zion-Branch four times for completions, including a 7-yard strike for TD. It was 14-7 with 2:05 left in the opening quarter.

Campos scored on a 13-yard run, but a holding penalty brought it back. An additional 15 yards was tacked on because Campos spiked the ball in the end zone. One play later, a sideline pass by Farley was intercepted to end the scoring threat.

After Loch Moorman fumbled on a first-down scramble, the Wolfpack drove 66 yards in 12 plays to the end zone. Two roughing-the-passer penalties and one pass-interference call against Kalaheo helped the 'Pack.

Shimabukuro's 5-yard TD pass to Zion-Branch on a slant tied the game at 14 with 3:39 left in the first half.

Kalaheo sputtered with a rash of penalties but still scored before the half. Campos' 2-yard run to the left pylon gave the Mustangs a 21-14 lead with 1:05 to go in the first half.

After an interception by Jayden Carreiro, Kalaheo drove 15 yards in five plays, scoring on Moorman's 5-yard run with six seconds left in the first half. That built a 28-14 cushion for the Mustangs.

The Mustangs amassed 10 penalties for 106 yards before halftime.

Kalaheo got a 34-yard kickoff return from Carreiro to set up a three-play, 40-play scoring drive. Moorman lofted a 13-yard TD pass to Storm Kane on a fade route. The Mustangs led 35-14 with 11:12 to go in the third quarter.

With showers drenching the premises occasionally, Kalaheo drove 46 yards and scored on Carreiro's 1-yard blast. It was 42-14 with 6:57 left in the third stanza.

Moments later, Kalaheo defensive end Coy Wallace hauled in a deflected pass and raced 33 yards for a TD. The PAT failed and it was 48-14 with 5:34 to go in the third quarter.

Zion-Branch still kept playing hard, hauling in a deep post pass from Shimabukuro, shaking off a tackler near midfield and turning on the jets for a 72-yard TD with 46 seconds left in the third quarter.

Campos' fourth TD, a 2-yard run, came with 8:39 remaining.

articles.body:
CLEVELAND (AP) — The Houston Texans will be short-handed when they try to keep their surge going on Sunday in Cleveland.

Edge rusher Danielle Hunter, wide receiver Marvin Harrison Jr., and running back David Montgomery will all sit out because of an injury. Three-time Pro Bowl left guard Wyatt Teller is dealing with an illness and will not play.

Hunter, who has four sacks this season, missed practice on Friday with a hamstring issue. Harrison, who is still trying to figure out his role after being acquired in a trade with Arizona, also has a hamstring injury.

Montgomery, listed as questionable on Friday's injury report, will miss his fourth straight game with a groin problem. Houston edge rusher Will Anderson, who had been questionable with an ankle injury, will play.

The Texans, who have won three of four since an 0-4 start, also made linebacker Azeez Al-Shaair, tight end Brevin Jordan and interior offensive lineman Keyland Rutledge inactive.

The Browns, coming off an overtime loss in New Orleans last week, made quarterbacks Dillon Gabriel and Taylen Green, linebacker Justin Jefferson, cornerback Noah Igbinoghene, safety Ronnie Hickman and center Parker Brailsford inactive.

On a wet night in Manoa, the Hawaii football team's postseason hopes appear to have slipped away.

North Dakota State scored 14 unanswered points in a 21-13 victory at the Ching Complex.

A crowd of 12,005 — it was announced as a sellout at 15,014 — saw the Rainbow Warriors fail to meet the minimum requirement for bowl eligibility this season. A .500 or better record is needed. The Warriors fell to 3-7 overall and 2-5 in the Mountain West with two games remaining.

The Warriors still could end up in a bowl if there are not enough qualifying teams. But that provided little consolation for the Warriors, who had dedicated the game to the memory of former head coach June Jones. Jones died on Oct. 28 in Portland.

"I don't know what the chances are," UH coach Timmy Chang said. "We can only control what we control."

Of the Warriors amassing only 262 yards and converting four of 17 on third down, Chang said, "We have to execute,We have to do better. I have to do better."

What had begun as a chaotic start for the Bison — their flight to Honolulu was delayed 13 hours because of mechanical problems on Thursday — turned into a festive finish. They brought about 2,000 fans.

The Bison took 16 plays to go 77 yards to take a 14-13 lead with 8:34 to play. Running back DJ Scott, behind an offensive line boosted with two tight ends and a fullback, scored from a yard out to tie it at 13. Despite being pushed back by a false start, Drew Klein converted the go-ahead, extra-point kick.

The Bison made it an eight-point difference when linebacker Ray James Jr. intercepted Micah Alejado and raced 49 yards for the touchdown. It was the Bison's fifth defensive touchdown of the season.

The Warriors could not catch up despite three ensuing possessions. The third was controversial. On a first-and-long, Alejado was called for intentional grounding. UH was penalized the lost yardage, as well as the down. But the sideline marker showed the next play was third down instead of second. After two incompletions, it appeared the Warriors had exhausted their final hope. But the referees then retroactively ruled that they miscalculated the downs.

UH was awarded a bonus fourth-and-19 play. Because Alejado was injured on the previous play, he was required to sit out a snap. Backup quarterback Bjorn Jurgensen scrambled for 6 yards and then stepped out of bounds, apparently unaware of the down-and-distance situation. The Bison took over on downs and, after quarterback Nathan Hayes took a knee, watched the clock run out.

"It's just tough, like we let our defense down, as an offense in general," UH center Ethan Spencer said. "We really need to pick things up for the last two games. We need to stick together. We need to make sure we keep working. We have two more guaranteed games left. We have to put everything into these last two."

The Bison are in their first season as members of both the FBS and the Mountain West. NDSU, which won 10 of 15 FCS championships through 2025, improved to 8-2 and 5-2.

The Warriors' defense set up Sean Olvera-Harle's two field goals in the third quarter.

UH nickelback Elijah Palmer tipped a second-down pass and then broke up the ensuing throw to force the Bison to punt. The Warriors then drove to the 10, leading to Olvera-Harle's 28-yard field goal to break a 7-all tie with 7:54 left in the third quarter.

Later, the Warriors' defensive stand forced the Bison to punt out of their end zone. On third-and-25, Cam Barfield ran 15 yards, setting up Olvera-Harle's field goal from 33 yards, increasing the UH advantage to 13-7 with 2:16 remaining in the third quarter.

The Bison had outscored opponents 59-9 in the third quarter of the first nine games. They were held scoreless in that quarter on Saturday.

Running on empty — minus-6 ground yards — for their first 30 offensive plays of the half, the Warriors came up with an imaginative call to tie it at 7 with four seconds left in the half.

After their fifth third-down stop of the half, the Warriors took over at their own 41. Alejado and slotback Kaikai Carvalho led the Warriors to the 15 with 18 seconds remaining. On fourth-and-3, the Warriors shuffled their backfield, with Alejado sliding to the side and running back DeVon Rice taking the direct snap from Spencer. Rice raced to his right, faked a handoff, followed fullback Sitani Mikaele's pancake block, and then used his 22.5 mph speed to sprint around the right corner and down the sideline for the 15-yard touchdown.

Olvera-Harle's extra-point kick tied it at 7-all.

Rice's TD gave the Warriors 9 rushing yards in the first half.

The Bison used defensive pressure to break a scoreless tie. Under a heavy attack, Alejado hurried a pass that Logan Larson intercepted at the Warriors' 11.

Two plays and 41 seconds later, Hayes lofted a pass to Mekhi Collins, who beat single coverage for a 7-yard scoring catch and a 7-0 NDSU lead with 4:20 left in the first quarter.

articles.title: Kirk Cousins is the first quarterback with 20 TD passes to change teams midseason
articles.summary: It was a crazy week for the Vikings and for quarterback Kirk Cousins.
articles.body:
It was a crazy week for the Vikings and for quarterback Kirk Cousins. The Tuesday trade that brought Cousins back to Minnesota three years after he played his last game for the Vikings has created a strange kind of history.

Cousins, per NBC Sports research, is the first quarterback with 20 touchdown passes to change teams during a season.

He ranks second in the league entering his first game with the Vikings, after nine games with the Raiders. And, given the placement of the byes, Cousins will be able to play in up to 18 games.

The most pressing question is whether the plug-and-play in purple will work. He ranked fourth in the league in passing yards (23,265) and touchdown passes (171) during his six years with Minnesota.

His return happens where his most recent game with the Vikings occurred; during Week 8 of the 2023 season, Cousins tore an Achilles tendon after throwing for 274 yards and two touchdown passes.

The bad news is that receiver Jordan Addison will miss Sunday's game with a thumb injury. During Cousins's last full game with the Vikings, he found Addison seven times for 123 yards and two touchdowns.

In that Monday night game against the 49ers, Cousins didn't have Justin Jefferson available. Jefferson is obviously available today, and the Cousins-to-Jefferson connection could be critical as to whether the Vikings can reverse a two-game losing streak.

articles.title: How FAA ground stop actually helped Utah’s Devon Dampier, Creed Whittemore in ‘high school’ throwback
articles.summary: Week 11 of the college football season saved the game of the week for last, as Utah and Arizona played an absolute epic deep into the night in Tucson. At the...
articles.body:
Week 11 of the college football season saved the game of the week for last, as Utah and Arizona played an absolute epic deep into the night in Tucson. At the end of the back-and-forth affair, the No. 2-ranked Utes escaped with a 40-39 win over the No. 23 Wildcats.

Utah overcame a lot on the field to get the win in this game, including a barrage of big plays from star Arizona quarterback Noah Fifita. But the Utes also had to get past some adversity off the field centered around their travel situation.

Friday's FAA ground stoppage impacted the travel plan s of a number of schools around the country, and Utah was among them. The Utes were slated to fly to Tucson on Friday afternoon, but were stranded by the grounding of flights. By the time the flight ban was lifted, Utah had already headed home to sleep in their own beds before flying out on Saturday morning.

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

According to star quarterback Devon Dampier and wide receiver Creed Whittemore, staying at home on Friday night may have actually helped the Utes out, per Ross Dellenger of Yahoo! Sports.

"Some of those hotel pillows are crazy!" Whittemore added.

It gave the Utes kind of a high-school feel. Whittemore's dad, a high school football coach, acknowledged that to his son on Saturday. Even despite the game getting moved back three hours to 10:30 p.m. EST, Utah was ready to play and put on one of their best offensive performances of the entire season.

"Taking it back to high school!" Whittemore laughed, per Dellenger.

Dampier didn't have his best day statistically, finishing 14-of-25 with 204 yards and two touchdowns with an interception. He also ran for 100 yards and two scores, and his playmaking ability in the pocket was one of the differences in the game in the end.

Whittemore led Utah in receiving, finishing this game with five catches for 92 yards and a touchdown. His 70-yard score on a perfect pass from Dampier with under three minutes left proved to be the difference that got Utah to 10-0.

articles.title: Timberwolves’ Chris Finch puts Rudy Gobert on blast after another embarrassing 0-fer shooting night
articles.summary: The Minnesota Timberwolves have been able to stay afloat this season with Anthony Edwards sidelined, but they recently took a tough loss against the Chicago...
articles.body:
The Minnesota Timberwolves have been able to stay afloat this season with Anthony Edwards sidelined, but they recently took a tough loss against the Chicago Bulls . One of the reasons for the loss is the lack of an interior presence, and that falls on Rudy Gobert , as he finished the game with 0 points, shooting 0-for-7 from the field.

It's been a rough season for Gobert finishing around the rim, and he had some bad moments against the Bulls.

After the game, head coach Chris Finch was asked why Gobert has been ineffective around the rim , and he didn't hold back on the center.

"Because he hasn't been able to finish. He's getting stripped, he's missing layups, he's not finishing strong. He's gotta get on balance, collect and finish strong. Sometimes it's gonna be through contact. We need him to get his finishing back around the paint," Finch said.

A few weeks ago, Finch mentioned Gobert not being able to get anything going when he finished their game against the Cleveland Cavaliers, shooting 0-for-9.

"We've got to find him a little more cleanly. We've not been able to do that. He's got to catch and finish better, he had 16 chances in and around the paint in the Cleveland game, didn't finish well. I think he's got to get back and play with a little bit more force down there and we have to find him a little cleaner at times," Finch said.

Gobert is usually the biggest person on the floor, and he has to do a better job of making his presence felt in the interior. If he can set the tone there, then that can open everything else up for the Timberwolves on the floor.
